items.excerpt: Friedrich Schiller University Jena researchers built '2-step', an AI tool that predicts when small molecules elute from liquid chromatography columns by first predicting retention order, then mapping it to times via reference compounds — outperforming prior methods without heavy retraining for new lab setups.
items.title: Ai method retention small molecules

items.excerpt: HUN-REN Biological Research Center's MALVINA uses machine learning on microscopy images to measure bacterial invasion, intracellular accumulation and induced DNA damage in human cells at single-cell resolution, for diagnostics, drug development and probiotic screening.
items.title: Machine bacterial invasion dna human

items.excerpt: A three-year study of nearly 8,000 Dutch elementary pupils found adaptive AI learning systems modestly improved arithmetic performance, but researchers stress the human teacher remains essential.
items.title: Math slightly ai human teacher

items.excerpt: A new machine-learning "speech clock" estimates a person's chronological age from their speech, drawing links between older-sounding speech and cognitive decline.
items.title: Your voice may reveal how fast you

items.excerpt: An attempt by Anthropic's Claude failed to prove the Riemann hypothesis, but it did produce something genuinely useful: inspiration.
items.title: This is what happened with claude and me ais failed attempt to crack the riemann hypothesis led mathematician to a breakthrough

items.excerpt: Researchers developed an AI system that beat human experts at the board wargame Stratego and outperformed more expensive models. This new system could someday help humans make strategic decisions in situations when some information is hidden.
items.title: This game-playing AI is the new champ at Stratego

items.excerpt: The use of a single hiring algorithm by multiple firms, known as algorithmic monoculture, is less problematic for job seekers than past research has shown, and may even be a good thing depending on the approach used, according to a study by MIT researchers.
items.title: The effects of an “algorithmic monoculture” depend on the details

items.excerpt: In the book 'How AI Sees the City,' MIT Senseable City Lab researchers examine using visual AI on street imagery to study urban life — more images mean more data and insight, but also privacy and fairness concerns.
items.title: The promise and peril of using visual AI to study cities

items.excerpt: Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions.
items.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology

items.excerpt: Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives:
items.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids

items.excerpt: Google DeepMind introduced SynthID Bio, function-preserving invisible watermarks for AI-designed proteins (published in Nature), letting AI-generated biological sequences be traced for provenance without degrading function.
items.title: SynthID Bio: Watermarking methods for synthetic biology — Google DeepMind

items.excerpt: Talus Bio unveiled Ptarmigan-1, a structure-free AI model that targets disordered/unstructured proteins in their native cellular context; internal benchmarks show it runs 5,000x faster than structure-based methods and screens over three billion compounds a day.
items.title: Talus Bio’s Structure-Free AI Model Targets Unstructured Proteins in Their Native Cellular Context

items.excerpt: Stanford geneticist Euan Ashley writes that analyzing his whole genome took 30 people and nearly a year in 2009; in 2026 Anthropic's Claude did it in 30 minutes for about $5 — and argues the field now needs standards for AI genome interpretation.
items.title: Claude analyzed my genome in 30 minutes. Now we need standards for the results

items.excerpt: UCLA researchers built an optical AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos at once, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy at low energy cost and with resistance to adversarial attacks.
items.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy

items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for protecting wildlife around the world
items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation – Physics World

items.excerpt: New research examines our emotional responses to AI companions — whether people feel they get to know an AI chatbot more easily than a human partner in conversation.
items.title: Who Is Easier to Get to Know: AI or Humans?

items.excerpt: A study comparing LLMs with human social scientists on theory formulation, prediction of novel empirical results and theory revision finds AIs and human scientists exhibit complementary strengths in theory building.
items.title: Artificial intelligences and human scientists exhibit complementary strengths in theory building

items.excerpt: AstroGenesis is a domain-specific multi-agent AI framework for astrophysical research that integrates literature retrieval, heterogeneous observational data and physical modeling into one research workflow.
items.title: AstroGenesis: A Domain-Specific Multi-Agent AI for Astrophysical Research

items.excerpt: 'Synthetic Universes' benchmark pairs canonical physical worlds with twisted twins governed by non-canonical laws to test whether AI scientist agents truly infer laws from evidence or merely recognize memorized ones.
items.title: Can AI Scientists Change Their Minds? Prior-Evidence Conflict in Synthetic Universes

items.excerpt: University of Miami researchers developed a quantum-inspired mathematical framework that helps AI systems recognize when they lack reliable information, testing stability of word-selection probabilities to flag unreliable answers in high-stakes uses like medicine.
items.title: Quantum math ai
